“Shirou…?”

Her languid voice comes through the door.

“Oh, please wait! I'll get dressed right away…!”

She must have been sleeping. I hear a sudden flurry of activity.

Then, perhaps two minutes later—

Even now, the thought of entering a girl's room makes me nervous.

I have been inside this room before, but the circumstances were different then.

Sakura was unconscious that time. Today she opened the door and invited me in herself.

“Oh, no, nothing like that. I didn't come because something happened. I was wondering whether you were resting properly, so I thought I'd check, but—”

The result is that I disturbed her sleep.

“Ahaha. Then I pass. I was resting properly, see?”

“Yeah. Sorry I woke you. You understand your own body, after all. You wouldn't run around pushing yourself with a fever. …I suppose I was being overprotective.”

My shoulders slump in remorse.

Sakura begins to giggle.

“No, not at all. You saw straight through me.

“The truth is, I wanted to finish the cleaning.

“If you hadn't come, I was thinking I might sneak out for a little while.”

“Hm… Sneak out? Sakura.”

“But then my sister got angry and told me not to be ridiculous.

“——”

Sakura rarely asks for anything.

Perhaps because she never wants to be a burden, she tries to manage almost everything alone.

And now Sakura is being selfish over something so small.

No—this is not selfishness at all, but to Sakura, it must feel like the greatest selfishness she has ever allowed herself.

As we pass, I pat her lightly on the head, then go to prepare the tea.

pages.en:
“…Sakura. Tohsaka is what you aspire to be?”

I ask with some trepidation.

If Tohsaka were here, the question might earn me one of those punches.

pages.ja:
「はい。ずっと姉さんみたいになりたいって思ってました。あ、もちろん魔術師としてじゃなく女の子としてですよ？
姉さんは何でもできて、いつも颯爽としてるじゃないですか。わたしも、一度でいいからあんな風にかっこよくなりたいなって」

pages.en:
“Yes. I always wanted to become like my sister. Oh, not as a mage, of course—as a girl.

“She can do anything, and she always carries herself with such confidence. Just once, I would like to be as impressive as she is.”

pages.ja:
嬉しそうに桜は語る。
……むむ。
そうなるとこっちとしては複雑な心境なのだが、まあ、たしかに遠坂はかっこいい。
自分の言動に責任を持つ、という点において、あいつはすごく男前だ。

pages.en:
Sakura speaks with delight.

…Hm.

That leaves me with rather complicated feelings, but she is right: Tohsaka is impressive.

When it comes to standing behind her own words and actions, no one cuts a more dashing figure.

pages.ja: 「……なるほど。けど、桜は今まで遠坂と会えなかったんだろう？ 間桐と遠坂の取り決めとかなんとかで。それでよく遠坂のこと知ってるな」

pages.en: “…I see. But you weren't allowed to meet Tohsaka, were you? Something about an agreement between the Matou and Tohsaka families. How do you know her so well?”

pages.ja:
「はい。だってどうしたって気になるじゃないですか。
わたしも姉さんも、子供の頃のことは覚えてないんです。
なにしろずっと前だったから。
ただ事実として、わたしたちは元々姉妹だったんだって知っていただけです」

pages.en:
“Because of course I was curious.

“Neither my sister nor I remember much from when we were children. It was so long ago.

“We only knew as a matter of fact that we had once been sisters.”

pages.ja:
「それで余計に気になって、わたしたちはお互いを遠くからよく見てたんです。

pages.en:
“That only made us more curious, so we often watched each other from a distance.

“We couldn't speak, but I heard plenty of stories about Tohsaka, the flawless model student one year above me.”

pages.ja:
「
ははあ。非の打ち所のない優等生って噂か。
言われてみれば、あいつは有名人だから話には事欠かないよな」

「

pages.en:
“—Ah. All those stories about the flawless model student.

“Now that you mention it, she's famous enough that you would never lack for news.”

pages.ja:
「はい。それに会えない、という事もありませんでした。
学校ではよく声をかけて貰えたし、弓道部にも見学に来てくれましたから」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Yes. And it isn't as though we never met at all.

“She often spoke to me at school, and she even came to observe the archery club.”

pages.ja: 「……それで、ですね。そういう時にいつも思ってたんです。わたしは見てもらえるだけでいいって。気にかけてもらえるだけで幸せだし、それ以上を望んだらきっと嫌われるってわかってましたから」

pages.en: “…And at those times, I always thought it was enough for her merely to see me. I was happy simply to know she cared. I knew that if I asked for anything more, she would surely come to hate me.”

pages.ja:
「……？ 嫌われるって、どうして？」

“…? Why would she hate you?”

“…My magecraft—the Matou art—is different from my sister's. Magecraft ordinarily has no fixed use, does it?

“Even your magecraft causes some phenomenon in order to accomplish something. It does not possess a single predetermined ‘purpose’ from the beginning.”

pages.ja: 「ん……そうだな。できる事は決まってるけど、強化をどう扱うかはその都度違う」
pages.jaRuby: 「ん……そうだな。できる事は決まってるけど、[ruby text=できたもの char=2]強化をどう扱うかはその都度違う」
pages.en: “Hm… Right. What I can do is fixed, but how I use the thing I've Reinforced changes each time.”

pages.ja:
「……けど間桐の魔術は違います。間桐の業は、初めから“他人から奪うこと”に限定した魔術なんです。
それ以外の用途なんて持たない。他人の痛みしか糧にせず、他人の喜びを還元する教えがない」

pages.en:
“…But Matou magecraft is different. The Matou art is restricted from the beginning to ‘taking from others.’

“It has no other use. It feeds upon nothing but the pain of others, and contains no teaching by which their happiness might be returned.”

pages.ja:
「…………」
そうか、なんて頷く事もできない。
桜が間桐でどんな魔術を教え込まれたのか、俺は知らない。
桜が教え込まれた魔術は外道の類で、それを桜自身が恥じている。

pages.en:
“…………”

I cannot even nod and say that I understand.

I do not know what magecraft the Matou family forced Sakura to learn.

But it belonged to the vilest kind of heresy, and Sakura herself is ashamed of it.

pages.ja:
……桜と遠坂の問題は、転じて両家の魔術の違いな訳だ。
桜が間桐の魔術を忌み嫌えば嫌うほど、桜は自分に対して嫌悪感を抱いてしまう

pages.en:
…The problem between Sakura and Tohsaka is, in another form, the difference between the magecraft of their two families.

The more Sakura loathes Matou magecraft, the more she comes to loathe herself—

pages.ja:
「桜は、間桐の魔術が嫌いなのか」
「先輩。それは人間に、呼吸をするのが嫌いなのかと訊いてるようなものです」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Do you hate Matou magecraft, Sakura?”

“Shirou, that is like asking a person whether she hates breathing.”

pages.ja:

」

pages.en:
“I neither like it nor dislike it. I simply could not have lived without doing as I was taught.

“I was given to the Matou family for that purpose alone. Had I failed to become their heir, I would have vanished then and there.”

“——”

pages.ja: 「あ。先輩、そんな顔しないでください。たしかに教えは厳しかったけど、先輩が思っているほど辛いものではなかったんですから」
pages.jaRuby: 「あ。先輩、そんな顔しないでください。たしかに教えは厳しかったけど、先輩が思っているほど辛いものではなかったんですから」
pages.en: “Oh. Please don't look like that, Shirou. Their instruction was harsh, but it wasn't nearly as painful as you imagine.”

pages.ja:
「それにですね、厳しさで言ったら先輩には敵いません。
わたし、人に傷つけられるのは楽なんですけど、自分で自分を傷つけるのは怖いんです。

pages.en:
“Besides, when it comes to harshness, I can't compare with you.

“It's easy when someone else hurts me, but I'm afraid to hurt myself.

“I cling too strongly to life to bring down the curtain with my own hands.

“Dying itself doesn't trouble me, but the thought of choosing my own death terrifies me.”

pages.en:
“But you can do both, Shirou. …I once saw the kind of training you perform at night.

“O-only once. I came back for something I had forgotten, heard a sound from the shed, and went to see what it was.”

pages.ja:
申し訳なさそうに頭を下げる桜。
が、そんなことで謝られてもこっちが困る。
pages.jaRuby:
申し訳なさそうに頭を下げる桜。
が、そんなことで謝られてもこっちが困る。
pages.en:
Sakura bows her head apologetically.

But an apology for something like that only leaves me at a loss.

pages.ja: 「いや、謝らなくていい。それは俺の不注意だろ。桜がいるって事に気付かなかったんだからな。周りの気配に気付けないようじゃ魔術師として失格だ」
pages.jaRuby: 「いや、謝らなくていい。それは俺の不注意だろ。桜がいるって事に気付かなかったんだからな。周りの気配に気付けないようじゃ魔術師として失格だ」
pages.en: “You don't need to apologize. It was my carelessness. I failed to notice you were there. A mage who can't sense someone nearby is a failure.”

pages.ja:
「……………………あの、それが」
「それより、それっていつの事だ？ 桜がやってくるようになってからすぐか？」
というか、すぐであってほしい。

pages.en:
“……………………Um. About that…”

“More importantly, when was this? Soon after you started coming here?”

Or rather, I desperately hope it was soon after.

My progress may be glacial, but even I have improved somewhat.

If I failed to notice Sakura's presence recently, then I haven't advanced at all since the old days.

「
そうか、良かった」

pages.en:
“…It was around last summer. The day Ms. Fujimura brought us a watermelon.”

“—Oh. Good.”

I sigh with relief.

If it was half a year ago, I can at least offer myself a little excuse.

pages.ja:

人に魔術の鍛錬を見られたのは、切嗣以外ではこれが初めてだ。

pages.en:
“…So, Sakura. Um… what did you think of what you saw?”

Other than Kiritsugu, no one has ever watched me train in magecraft.

I have practiced before Tohsaka over the last several days, but that was very different from my training in the shed.

pages.en:
That makes Sakura's opinion feel rather like the mark on an examination.

“Um. As for the content, I'll exercise my right to remain silent. I may not be my sister, but if I gave you a grade, it would be disastrous.”

“Urgh—does that mean I failed?”

“Ahaha. You could call it a spectacular failure.”

pages.en:
“——”

…I give up.

For all that she seems unlike her sister, Sakura can be remarkably similar.

pages.ja:

「？ 怖くて見られなかった……？」
pages.jaRuby:
「けど先輩？ わたし、本当にその時しか見てないんです。……いえ、見てないんじゃなくて、怖くてもう見られなかった」
「？ 怖くて見られなかった……？」
pages.en:
“But Shirou, that truly was the only time I watched. …No, it wasn't that I chose not to. I was too frightened to look again.”

“Hm? Too frightened…?”

pages.en:
“Yes. More than that, I thought again and again that I had to stop you.

“…Your training isn't normal. To me, it looked as though you were driving a blade into your own throat. I don't mean I imagined it—I could truly see it happening. …Your training was dangerous enough to make the illusion real.”

pages.ja:
桜の言いたい事は判る。
俺にとって、魔術回路を発現させる事は死に近い行為だった。

pages.en:
I understand what Sakura means.

For me, manifesting a Magic Circuit was an act close to death.

If the concentration stretched throughout my body slipped by even a millimeter, everything inside me would be blown apart.

But isn't that an ordinary price for a mage?

Dad always said magecraft meant living beside death.

pages.ja:
「
そうかな。魔術師ならあんなものだって聞いてるけど。それに俺が危なっかしいのは、単にまだ未熟だからじゃないか」
pages.jaRuby:
「

pages.en: “—Is it really so strange? I was told that's what being a mage is like. Besides, the danger probably only came from my being inexperienced.”

pages.ja:
「それは違います。未熟とか半人前とか、そういう話ではないんです。だいたい、そんな事を言ったら資質がないのに魔術を使える先輩は別格です。

“No. It has nothing to do with being inexperienced or half-trained. If anything, the fact that you can use magecraft without the proper aptitude makes you exceptional.

“Magecraft is not something one simply uses. It is something the body learns. An ordinary mage does not manifest a Magic Circuit anew every time, solely to perform magecraft, the way you do.”

“…?”

“I am speaking about the final result.

“…Every night, you were killing yourself. No one forced you. You weren't even doing it for yourself. Yet you continued alone, stubbornly keeping to that practice.”

“…I don't think even my sister could do that.

“Whether what you choose is good or evil, once you decide upon it, you keep faith with it until the end. That is why you may be the strongest among us.”

“No. You are strong, Shirou. Not because of your Magic Circuits or any property of your magecraft, but because the shape of your heart is pure.

“…I knew that from the moment we met.

“I thought: this is someone who will never betray anything.”

“Ah————well…”

When she says it so earnestly, with that expression, I cannot possibly argue.

照れながらも、素直な気持ちを口にする。
桜は、
幸せそうに笑って、まっすぐに俺を見つめていた。

pages.en:
“…Thanks. Even if it's only flattery, hearing you say that makes me very happy.”

Embarrassed, I nevertheless speak honestly.

Sakura smiles with perfect happiness and looks straight into my eyes.

pages.ja:

まずい。
そんな顔をされると、さっき振り払った妄念が再発してしまう。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…………!”

This is bad.

When she looks at me that way, the desires I drove away a moment ago come rushing back.

こほん、とわざとらしく咳なんぞをしてみる。

“…Um. I should probably go back now. You're tired, aren't you? We still have tonight ahead of us, so you ought to spend the afternoon resting quietly.”

I produce an exaggerated cough.

My gaze strays next door—toward Tohsaka and Illya, only one wall away.

「そ、そうですね。夜もありますし、隣りには姉さんがいるんだし」
こっちの気持ちを分かってくれたのか、桜は頬を赤らめてごにょごにょと口にする。
……自分で言っておいてなんだが、きっとこっちもあんな顔をしてるんだろう。

“Y-yes. We still have tonight, and my sister is right next door.”

Perhaps understanding what I mean, Sakura blushes and mumbles the words.

…I was the one who said it, but I'm sure my face looks much the same.

“I'll go back to my room, then. I'll come for you when dinner is ready.”

“Ah—um, wait, Shirou…!”

“Hm? I'll wait. What is it?”

途切れ途切れの言葉に、思わず苦笑してしまった。
そんな事、むしろこっちがお願いしたいぐらいだ。

pages.en:
“Um… well, I would be happy if you stayed until I fell asleep…”

Her halting request draws an involuntary smile from me.

If anything, I'm the one who would like to ask for that.

pages.ja: 「ああ。邪魔じゃなかったらここにいる。桜が眠ったら出て行くから、それでいいかな」
pages.jaRuby: 「ああ。邪魔じゃなかったらここにいる。桜が眠ったら出て行くから、それでいいかな」
pages.en: “All right. If I won't disturb you, I'll stay. I'll leave after you fall asleep. Is that all right?”

だから桜。
そう言ってくれるのは嬉しいんだが、それじゃ意味がないんだってば。

“Y-yes, of course! I'll do my best to stay awake!”

Sakura.

I'm delighted that you feel that way, but that defeats the point.

The moment Sakura lies down, she becomes quiet.

She must have been terribly exhausted. Sleep seems to overwhelm her the instant her body touches the bed.

And yet, despite that—

“But Shirou, I'll be better after resting for one day. What about your arm?”

Apparently she has no intention of going quietly to sleep. Even lying in bed, Sakura continues talking to me.

pages.en: “My arm is fine. As long as this cloth remains wrapped around it, there's no pain, and little by little, it's beginning to move again. At this rate, it may be working normally by tomorrow.”

“Won't last… seven days?”

“…Shirou, you're still there, aren't you?”

“Yes. I'm right here.”

“…I'm glad. Stay beside me, Shirou.

“Whenever I'm alone, all I see are frightening dreams. So please, keep—”

…Her eyes close slowly.

Breathing peacefully, Sakura descends into a deep sleep.

I turn off the light and quietly leave the guest room.

“……………………”

Though I saw Sakura sleeping so peacefully, something dark and clouded remains in my chest.
